Hi Nikhil,

We just reviewed our May invoice and noticed a line with a fairly large delta coming from "micro-call" usage. The total token volume on the invoice looks consistent with our internal logs, but the billed units for short-lived calls near the 1-3 token responses seem to be rounding up much more aggressively than expected.

Can you explain how the rounding/proration is being applied at the per-request level? Specifically:
- Are short calls being billed to the minimum session quantum or to a per-call quantum?
- How does prefix reuse / KV-cache hit factor into the rounding?
- Is there any rounding applied after aggregation across the billing window that could cause us to see a larger-than-expected delta?

We've attached the invoice (invoice_May2026_LintelHealth.pdf) and sampled a few request IDs from our logs. Happy to share more if that helps — Sam and I are trying to reconcile the spike before we process payment.

Hi Ellie — thanks for the note and for attaching the invoice. Sorry for the stress here; I want to get you a clear, line-by-line explanation so you and Sam can close this out quickly.

Short answers up front:
- By default we bill per-token but apply a minimum quantum for very short calls. There are two places rounding can appear: at the individual request level (we round to the per-call quantum), and at the invoice aggregation step (we sum all rounded units).
- Prefix/KV cache hits reduce compute tokens but do not retroactively change already-applied per-call rounding.
- We do have an aggregation step that can cause a small mismatch vs raw token sum, especially when you have many tiny calls.

To reconcile this I need a short sampled trace from you: a CSV with request_id, timestamp, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, model, and whether the KV cache hit. If you can't provide that, we can also pull a token trace on our side using the request ids you mentioned.

I'll loop in Karthik and Marissa to share the exact math we used for May and a short worked example. In parallel, we can propose a one-off smoothing credit if this turns out to be an edge-case of many tiny calls.

Best,

Morning all — looping in the billing playbook details. Ellie, thanks for the example — that made this easier to debug. Below is a compact explanation and a couple of concrete examples.

Summary of how May was computed (short version):
1) Per request we measure prompt_tokens and completion_tokens (raw counts).
2) We convert to billable units using token_unit = ceil((prompt_tokens + completion_tokens) / quantum_size). Quantum_size for the account in May was 16 tokens (per your contractual SKU).
3) A per-call minimum floor is applied after the ceil (we currently enforce a min of 1 quantum per call when usage > 0).
4) At invoice time we sum all per-call billable quanta into an invoice line; we do not recompute a ceil on the aggregated raw token sum.

Why you can see a delta: if you have 1,000 calls of 2 tokens each, per-call you get ceil(2/16)=1 quantum => billed as 1,000 quanta. If we aggregated first: ceil(2000/16)=125 quanta — large difference. That pattern explains the spike you saw.

KV-cache notes: KV hits reduce prompt_tokens for the call (so they reduce the numerator). However, they don't remove the per-call ceil floor — a call with a cache hit that results in 1 token response will still round to 1 quantum.

Attached: a small CSV (token_trace_sample.csv) with anonymized request-level examples and a short worked calculation. Also attached the internal pricing_playbook_v2.docx excerpt describing the aggregation rule.

Proposal for reconciliation and to avoid recurrence:
- Short-term: we can issue a smoothing credit equal to the difference between per-call-quantized billing and an aggregated-first calculation for May. This would be a one-time concession tied to May 2026 (we can do a partial credit if you want to share which request ids to prioritize).
- Medium-term: we can enable an "aggregation-first" billing flag for your account on a pilot basis (limits: must be enabled for a whole billing period and is not backwards-compatible with previous invoices). This would prevent this rounding behavior going forward for small-call-heavy workloads.

If you'd like we'll coordinate a brief call to review sample traces and confirm the credit.
